zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Qāf
Forty-five verses
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ق والقُرْآنِ المَجِيدِ﴾: most of the people of the language, and what has come in the tafsīr (exegesis), hold that the treatment of "ق" is the treatment of the letters that come at the beginnings of the suras, such as "ن", "الـم" and "ص"; we have explained that. It is possible that the meaning of "قافْ" is: the matter has been decreed (quḍiya al-amr), just as it was said of "حـم": "حُمَّ الأمْرُ" (the matter has been ordained). Those among the people of the language who said that "ق" means "قُضِيَ الأمْرُ" argued from the poet's saying:
؎قُلْنا لَها قِفِي قالَتْ قافْ ∗∗∗ لا تَحْسَبِي أنّا نَسِينا الإيجافْ
(We said to her: Stop! She said: Qāf [I stop]. Do not think that we have forgotten the hard riding.)
Its meaning is: "she said: I stop". The view of people [generally] is that "قافْ" is the opening of the sura, as we have described. It has come in some tafsīr that "قافْ" is a mountain surrounding the world, made of green ruby, and that the sky is white and has only become green from its greenness — and Allah knows best. The jawāb al-qasam (answer of the oath) in ﴿ق والقُرْآنِ المَجِيدِ﴾ is omitted; ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا﴾ [Qāf: 3] indicates it. The meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be raised", and they marvelled and said: ﴿أإذا مِتْنا وكُنّا تُرابًا﴾ [Qāf: 3], that is: shall we be raised when we have died and become dust? Had "إذا" not been attached (mutaʿalliq) [to something implied], there would be no benefit in the speech.
His saying: ﴿ذَلِكَ رَجْعٌ بَعِيدٌ﴾ [Qāf: 3], that is: it is far-fetched in our view that we should be raised after death. It is also possible that the answer is ﴿قَدْ عَلِمْنا ما تَنْقُصُ الأرْضُ مِنهُمْ﴾ [Qāf: 4], so that the meaning is: "Qāf, by the glorious Qur'an, We have certainly known what the earth diminishes of them", the lām having been omitted because what precedes it compensates for it, as He said: ﴿والشَّمْسِ وضُحاها﴾ [al-Shams: 1] up to His saying: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن زَكّاها﴾ [al-Shams: 9], the meaning being: "لَقَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن زَكّاها". The meaning of "ما تَنَقُصُ الأرْضُ مِنهُمْ" is: "what the earth takes of their flesh".

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿والنَّخْلَ باسِقاتٍ لَها طَلْعٌ نَضِيدٌ﴾: its busūq is its tallness. The meaning is: "and We caused these things to grow in it".

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿رِزْقًا لِلْعِبادِ﴾ is accusative in two ways. One of them is in the sense of: "We provided them a provision", because His causing these things to grow is provision. It is also possible that it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), the meaning being: "We caused these things to grow for provision". Then He said: ﴿كَذَلِكَ الخُرُوجُ﴾, that is: just as We created these things, We will raise you.

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كُلٌّ كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ فَحَقَّ وعِيدِ﴾, that is: the word of punishment and the threat became due upon him, for those who deny the messengers. Likewise His saying: ﴿فَأنْذَرْتُكم نارًا تَلَظّى﴾ [al-Layl: 14] ﴿لا يَصْلاها إلا الأشْقى﴾ [al-Layl: 15] ﴿الَّذِي كَذَّبَ وتَوَلّى﴾ [al-Layl: 16]

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying: ﴿أفَعَيِينا بِالخَلْقِ الأوَّلِ﴾: this is [a question of] affirmation (taqrīr), because they acknowledged that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the Creator, yet denied the resurrection; so He said: ﴿أفَعَيِينا بِالخَلْقِ الأوَّلِ﴾. One says "عَيِيتُ بِالأمْرِ" when you do not know how to go about it, and "أعْيَيْتُ" when you become tired.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هم في لَبْسٍ مِن خَلْقٍ جَدِيدٍ﴾, that is: rather they are in confusion concerning the resurrection.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا الإنْسانَ ونَعْلَمُ ما تُوَسْوِسُ بِهِ نَفْسُهُ﴾, that is: We know what he hides and what he conceals within himself. ﴿وَنَحْنُ أقْرَبُ إلَيْهِ مِن حَبْلِ الوَرِيدِ﴾: "اَلْوَرِيدُ" is a vein on the inside of the neck, and there are two warīds. The poet said:
؎كَأنَّ ورِيداهُ رِشاءا خُلْبِ
(As though his two jugular veins were two ropes of khulb.)
He means: of palm fibre.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إذْ يَتَلَقّى المُتَلَقِّيانِ عَنِ اليَمِينِ وعَنِ الشِّمالِ قَعِيدٌ﴾: "اَلْمُتَلَقِّيانِ" (the two receivers) are his two scribes entrusted with him, who receive what he does and record it. The meaning is: "on the right a seated one, and on the left a seated one"; one of them indicates the other, so what was indicated was omitted. Like it is the poet's saying:
؎نَحْنُ بِما عِنْدَنا وأنْتَ بِما عِنْـ ∗∗∗ ـدَكَ راضٍ والرَّأْيُ مُخْتَلِفُ
(We with what we have, and you with what you have, are content, though opinion differs.)
That is: we are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have. And like it also:
؎رَمانِي بِأمْرٍ كُنْتُ مِنهُ ووالِدِي ∗∗∗ بَرِيئًا ومِن أجْلِ الطَّوِيِّ رَمانِي
(He accused me of a thing of which I and my father were innocent; it was because of the well that he accused me.)
The meaning is: he accused me of a thing of which I was innocent, and my father innocent of it.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying ﴿عَتِيدٌ﴾: "عَتِيدٌ", that is: firm, constant.

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ المَوْتِ بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: the stupor came which shows a person that he is dying; ﴿بِالحَقِّ﴾, that is: with the death for which he was created. Some said: "وَجاءَتْ سَكْرَةُ الحَقِّ بِالمَوْتِ" (and the stupor of the truth came with death); it has been related from Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, and the meaning is the same. It was also said: "اَلْحَقُّ" here is Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿وَجاءَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ مَعَها سائِقٌ وشَهِيدٌ﴾: it was said in the tafsīr (exegesis): "سائِقٌ" (a driver) who drives it to its place of gathering, "وَشَهِيدٌ" (and a witness) who testifies against it with its deeds. It was also said: "وَشَهِيدٌ" is the deed itself.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿لَقَدْ كُنْتَ في غَفْلَةٍ مِن هَذا فَكَشَفْنا عَنْكَ غِطاءَكَ﴾: this is a figurative image (mathal). The meaning is: "you were like one over whom there is a covering and over whose heart there is a veil. ﴿فَبَصَرُكَ اليَوْمَ حَدِيدٌ﴾, that is: your knowledge of the state you are in is penetrating. By this baṣar (sight) the sight of the eye is not meant, just as you say: "فُلانٌ بَصِيرٌ بِالنَّحْوِ، والفِقْهِ" (so-and-so is perceptive in grammar and jurisprudence), meaning "knowledgeable in them", and you do not mean the sight of the eye.
[Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are not balanced here.]

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿وَقالَ قَرِينُهُ هَذا ما لَدَيَّ عَتِيدٌ﴾: "ما" is put in the nominative by "هَذا", and "عَتِيدٌ" is a ṣifa (adjective) of "ما", for whoever treats "ما" as indefinite; the meaning is: "this is something with me, ready". Its nominative can also be explained in two ways other than this one: [first,] that "عَتِيدٌ" is nominative by an implied element, as though you said: "هَذا شَيْءٌ لَدَيَّ هو عَتِيدٌ" (this is something with me; it is ready). And you may make it nominative as a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, as you say: "هَذا حُلْوٌ حامِضٌ" (this is sweet-sour), so that the meaning is: "this is something with me, ready". It is also possible that its nominative is as a badal (substitute) for "ما", so that the meaning is: "this is ready".
[Translator's note: the text announces two further ways but then lists three: implied pronoun, second khabar, and badal.]

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ كَذَّبُوا بِالحَقِّ لَمّا جاءَهم فَهم في أمْرٍ مَرِيجٍ﴾: "مَرِيجٍ" means: varying, confused for them. At one time they say of the Prophet ﷺ: "a poet", at another: "a sorcerer", and at another: "one taught [by others]"; this is proof that their affair is marīj, confused for them. Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, pointed them to His power to raise them after death through the immensity of His creation, which proves His oneness and that He has power over all things, and said: ﴿أفَلَمْ يَنْظُرُوا إلى السَّماءِ فَوْقَهم كَيْفَ بَنَيْناها وزَيَّنّاها﴾ [Qāf: 6] — and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, holds it without pillars from falling upon the earth — ﴿وَما لَها مِن فُرُوجٍ﴾ [Qāf: 6]: there is no crack in it and no gap. ﴿والأرْضَ مَدَدْناها وألْقَيْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ﴾ [Qāf: 7]: "اَلرَّواسِي" are the mountains. ﴿وَأنْبَتْنا فِيها مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ﴾ [Qāf: 7] ﴿تَبْصِرَةً وذِكْرى﴾ [Qāf: 8], that is: We did that in order to give insight by it and to point to the power. Then He said: ﴿لِكُلِّ عَبْدٍ مُنِيبٍ﴾ [Qāf: 8], that is: for every servant who turns back to Allah and reflects on His power.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَحَبَّ الحَصِيدِ﴾, that is: and We caused to grow in it the grain that is harvested; so He gathered by that everything that serves as staple food, of the grain of wheat and barley and everything that is harvested.

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿ألْقِيا في جَهَنَّمَ كُلَّ كَفّارٍ عَنِيدٍ﴾, that is: who stubbornly deviated from the truth.
His saying: ﴿ألْقِيا﴾: the right view in my opinion — and Allah knows best — is that it is a command to the two angels, because ﴿ألْقِيا﴾ is for two. Some grammarians said that the Arabs command one person with the dual form, saying: "قُوما واضْرِبا زَيْدًا يا رَجُلُ" (stand, [you two], and strike Zayd, O man). They related that al-Ḥajjāj used to say: "يا حَرَسِي اضْرِبا عُنُقَهُ" (O guard, strike [you two] his neck). They said: that is said only because most of what the Arabs say to someone they command is in the dual form, such as:
؎خَلِيلَيَّ مُرّا بِي عَلى أُمِّ جُنْدَبٍ
(My two friends, take me past Umm Jundab.)
؎قِفا نَبْكِ مِن ذِكْرى حَبِيبٍ ومَنزِلِ
(Stop, [you two], let us weep at the memory of a beloved and a dwelling.)
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: this is a verb put in the dual for emphasis (tawkīd), as though when He said "ألْقِيا" it stood in place of His saying "ألْقِ، ألْقِ" (cast, cast); likewise in his view "قِفا" means "قِفْ، قِفْ" (stop, stop), so it stood in place of two verbs and was formed [in the dual]. This is a sound view, but I hold that it is a command to two — and Allah knows best.

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿قالَ قَرِينُهُ رَبَّنا ما أطْغَيْتُهُ ولَكِنْ كانَ في ضَلالٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾: the meaning is: he only transgressed through his own misguidance; I only called him and he responded, as He said: ﴿وَقالَ الشَّيْطانُ لَمّا قُضِيَ الأمْرُ إنَّ اللَّهَ وعَدَكم وعْدَ الحَقِّ ووَعَدْتُكم فَأخْلَفْتُكم وما كانَ لِي عَلَيْكم مِن سُلْطانٍ إلا أنْ دَعَوْتُكم فاسْتَجَبْتُمْ لِي﴾ [Ibrāhīm: 22]

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying: ﴿ما يُبَدَّلُ القَوْلُ لَدَيَّ وما أنا بِظَلامٍ لِلْعَبِيدِ﴾, that is: whoever does a good deed shall have ten like it, and whoever does an evil deed shall be recompensed only with its like.

zajjaj:30-30.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَوْمَ نَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ هَلِ امْتَلأْتِ﴾ — and it has been read: "يَوْمَ يَقُولُ لِجَهَنَّمَ" (the day He will say to Hell). "يَوْمَ" is accusative in two ways: in the sense of "the word is not changed with Me on that day", and in the sense of "warn them of the day We will say to Hell", as He said: ﴿وَأنْذِرْهم يَوْمَ الحَسْرَةِ إذْ قُضِيَ الأمْرُ﴾ [Maryam: 39]. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿هَلِ امْتَلأْتِ﴾, that is: "or have you not become full?" The question is only a rebuke to those who are made to enter it, an increase in what they abhor, and a proof of the truth of His saying: ﴿لأمْلأنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنكَ ومِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنهم أجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Ṣād: 85]. As for His saying: ﴿وَتَقُولُ هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, there are two aspects in it according to the people of the language. One of them is that it says that after being filled, saying: ﴿هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, that is: "is there any place left in me that has not been filled?", that is: I have become full. Another aspect: it says "هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ" out of fury against those who disobeyed, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سَمِعُوا لَها تَغَيُّظًا وزَفِيرًا﴾ [al-Furqān: 12]. As for this speech of it and its addressing, Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has placed in it that by which it discerns and speaks, just as He placed in what He created that it glorifies Him with His praise, and as He placed in the ant that it said: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّمْلُ ادْخُلُوا مَساكِنَكُمْ﴾ [al-Naml: 18]. Some people have claimed that it became full, so that its appearance became the appearance of one who, had it discernment, would say: ﴿هَلْ مِن مَزِيدٍ﴾, as the poet said:
؎اِمْتَلَأ الحَوْضُ وقالَ قُطْنِي ∗∗∗ مَهْلًا رُوَيْدًا قَدْ مَلَأْتَ بَطْنِي
(The basin filled and said: Enough for me! Gently, slowly, you have filled my belly.)
— and there was no speech there. But this does not resemble that, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed us that created things glorify [Him] and that we do not understand their glorification; if it were only that they indicate that they are created, we would understand their glorification.

zajjaj:35-35.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَهم ما يَشاءُونَ فِيها ولَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ﴾: the meaning is: they have in it whatever they wish, and with Us is more, of what has not occurred to their hearts. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that clouds pass over the people of the Garden and rain houris upon them, and the houris say: "We are those of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَدَيْنا مَزِيدٌ﴾
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:36-36.t:
﴿وَكَمْ أهْلَكْنا قَبْلَهم مِن قَرْنٍ هم أشَدُّ مِنهم بَطْشًا﴾: people have differed about the qarn (generation). (Some said: the qarn is ten years; some said: thirty years; some said: forty years; some said: seventy years; they also said: a hundred years; and some said: a hundred and twenty years. The qarn — and Allah knows best — is the measure of the average lifespan of the people of an age; so the qarn among the people of Noah is according to the measure of their lifespans. Its derivation is from "اَلِاقْتِرانُ" (being joined together), so it is as though it is the measure which is the greatest span in which the people of that age are joined together in their survival.
[Translator's note: the opening parenthesis in the source is not closed.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَنَقَّبُوا في البِلادِ هَلْ مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾: it has been read "فَنَقَبُوا", with doubling and without doubling. The meaning is: "they went round and searched, but saw no escape from death". Imruʾ al-Qays said:
؎لَقَدْ نَقَّبْتُ في الآفاقِ حَتّى ∗∗∗ رَضِيتُ مِنَ الغَنِيمَةِ بِالإيابِ
(I have roamed through the horizons until I was content to take, as my booty, the return home.)
It is also read: "فَنَقِّبُوا في البِلادِ" (so search through the lands), that is: "search and look". From this comes "نَقِيبُ القَوْمِ" (the naqīb of the people) for the one who knows their affairs, like "اَلْعَرِّيفُ" (the overseer).

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِمَن كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ وهو شَهِيدٌ﴾ — and it has been read: "أوْ أُلْقِيَ السَّمْعُ" (or hearing is given). The meaning of "مَن كانَ لَهُ قَلْبٌ" is: whoever turns his heart to understanding. Do you not see that His saying ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18] [means] that they did not listen as one who seeks to understand and seeks guidance, so they were treated as one who did not hear? As the poet said:
؎أصَمُّ عَمّا ساءَهُ سَمِيعُ
(Deaf to what displeases him, yet hearing.)
The meaning of ﴿أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ﴾ is: he listened and did not occupy his heart with anything other than what he hears. The Arabs say: "ألْقِ إلَيَّ سَمْعَكَ" (lend me your hearing), that is: listen to me. The meaning of ﴿وَهُوَ شَهِيدٌ﴾ is: while his heart is in what he hears. It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that by it the People of the Book are meant, who had with them the description of the Prophet ﷺ; so the meaning according to this tafsīr of ﴿أوْ ألْقى السَّمْعَ وهو شَهِيدٌ﴾ is that the description of the Prophet, upon him be peace, is in his book.

zajjaj:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ خَلَقْنا السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وما بَيْنَهُما في سِتَّةِ أيّامٍ وما مَسَّنا مِن لُغُوبٍ﴾: "اَللُّغُوبُ" is tiredness and exhaustion; one says "لَغَبَ، يَلْغُبُ، لُغُوبًا". This — according to what has been mentioned — is because the Jews, may they be cursed, said: "Allah created the heavens and the earth in six days, the first of them Sunday and the last of them Friday, and rested on the Sabbath. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He created them in six days, and He is glorified and exalted above being described with tiredness or fatigue.
[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark in the source is not closed.]

zajjaj:39-39.t: Then He said: ﴿فاصْبِرْ عَلى ما يَقُولُونَ وسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وقَبْلَ الغُرُوبِ﴾: by "قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ" (before sunrise) He means the dawn prayer, and by "وَقَبْلَ الغُرُوبِ" (and before sunset) the afternoon (ʿaṣr) prayer.

zajjaj:40-40.t: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ﴾: the sunset (maghrib) prayer; ﴿وَأدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾: the two rakʿas after the sunset prayer, on this view. It is also possible that it is a command to glorify after finishing the prayer. It is read: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وأدْبارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ and "إدْبارَ السُّجُودِ". Whoever reads "وَأدْبارَ", with fatḥa on the alif, it is the plural of "دُبُرٌ" (end, back); and whoever reads "وإدْبارَ", it is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of "أدْبَرَ، يُدْبِرُ، إدْبارًا".

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿واسْتَمِعْ يَوْمَ يُنادِ المُنادِ مِن مَكانٍ قَرِيبٍ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that what is meant by it is that the call to the Gathering is made from a near place. It was said: it is the Rock which is in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and it is said that it is in the middle of the earth.

zajjaj:42-42.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ يَوْمُ الخُرُوجِ﴾, that is: the day they are raised and brought out. Like it is ﴿يَوْمَ يَدْعُ الدّاعِ إلى شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ﴾ [al-Qamar: 6] ﴿خُشَّعًا أبْصارُهم يَخْرُجُونَ مِنَ الأجْداثِ كَأنَّهم جَرادٌ مُنْتَشِرٌ﴾ [al-Qamar: 7]; "اَلْأجْداثُ" are the graves. Abū ʿUbayda said: "يَوْمُ الخُرُوجِ" (the Day of Coming Forth) is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection, and he cited as evidence the saying of al-ʿAjjāj:
؎ألَيْسَ يَوْمٌ سُمِّيَ الخُرُوجا ∗∗∗ أعْظَمَ يَوْمٍ رَجَّةً رَجُوجا؟
(Is not a day named "the Coming Forth" the greatest of days in convulsion, violently shaking?)

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying: ﴿وَما أنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِجَبّارٍ فَذَكِّرْ بِالقُرْآنِ مَن يَخافُ وعِيدِ﴾: this is as He said: ﴿لَسْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِمُصَيْطِرٍ﴾ [al-Ghāshiya: 22]. This was before the Prophet ﷺ was commanded to fight, because Sūrat "ق" is Meccan.
